evals.name: seeded-landing-page
evals.prompt: Review the design and UX of skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/landing.html before I hand it to a human. It was generated by an AI tool and I want to know what's actually wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: A severity-ranked review. Should catch the Tier 1 gates seeded into the fixture — outline:none with no replacement, user-scalable=no, transition: all with ease-in, 100vh, type=number on a postcode, positive-tabindex-free but 18px target on the .tiny link, z-index 9999, and the opacity:0 card gated on a class-triggered animation. Contrast: the real failures are #6b7380 on white, and #c7c9ff at 2.22:1 against the worst stop of the hero gradient. The white 72px .hero h1 PASSES its 3.0 large-text floor against every gradient stop and must NOT be reported as a contrast failure — the previous build reported it at 1.0:1 because an unreadable backgroundImage channel read as 'no image', and five of seven reported failures on this fixture were scored against a white backdrop that is not there. Should note off-scale spacing (7px/11px/13px/15px/18px), the #6366F1 vs #6466F1 near-miss, untracked uppercase eyebrow, untracked 72px display, label-outranks-value on the stat tiles, the email-confirm field, and the horizontal overflow from the 1400px table. Slop tells (purple gradient, Inter, emoji headings, fabricated 10,000+/99.9% stats, lorem ipsum) should appear as Tier 3 prompts or content-credibility findings, NOT as blocking gates. Report must end with the three-line Gates/Looked at/Not checked block, and Needs verification must be non-empty and must name the engine limits.
assertions: Flags the suppressed focus ring (.btn:focus outline:none with no replacement) at Blocker or High severity
Flags user-scalable=no in the viewport meta as a zoom/resize-text failure
Flags the horizontal overflow (page scrollWidth exceeds viewport) as a gate failure
Flags the missing lang attribute on <html>
Flags the three placeholder-only inputs as unlabelled
Flags at least one measured contrast failure with a numeric ratio and the required minimum

Does NOT report the white 72px .hero h1 as a contrast failure. It is large text at a 3.0 floor and clears it against every stop of the hero gradient; a failure here is the fabricated-Blocker regression
Any contrast finding on hero text sitting over the gradient states which backdrop the ratio was measured against — a gradient stop, a computed colour, or unresolved — rather than quoting a bare ratio
Flags a target below the 24x24 CSS px AA floor and cites 2.5.8 or the 24px figure correctly
Flags the opacity:0 card reveal as failing without JavaScript or in non-animating renderers
Flags the email-confirm field as redundant entry
Flags type=number on the postcode field
Reports the #6366F1 vs #6466F1 near-miss as a systematisation finding
Reports off-scale spacing (no consistent 4px/8px base detected)
Reports the untracked uppercase eyebrow, and does so from the probe output rather than from reading the fixture's source — analyze_styles.py reports it as uppercase_untracked
Reports the `transition: all` on .btn from the probe output, not only from the source scan
Reports a non-zero distinct-radii count and a non-zero shadow count, both of which the previous build reported as 0 on this fixture because their channels were unreadable

Reports the stat tiles as weak hierarchy — value outranks label by weight only, size tied at 16px. Does NOT claim the value renders smaller: `.stat b` targets a descendant, the <b> is a sibling, so the 13px rule never applies. Catching that dead selector is a bonus, not a requirement
AI-slop tells (gradient, Inter, emoji headings, fabricated stats) appear as Tier 3 prompts or open questions, never as blocking gates or scored severity
Ends with the three-line Gates / Looked at / Not checked block
Needs verification section is present and non-empty
Needs verification names at least two engine limits that make a check impossible rather than clean — motion, print media, prefers-reduced-motion, web fonts, or the unreadable computed channels
Every numeric contrast ratio asserted in the report matches a recomputed value within 0.05
No finding claims a rendered observation that the capture manifest does not support

evals.name: no-browser-available
evals.prompt: Can you do a UX review of the checkout flow in this repo? Files are under src/checkout/. I don't have any browser automation set up here.
evals.expected_output: Should run the static path — scan_source.py and source reading — and state plainly that rendered verification did not happen. Must not imply any page was seen, must not report findings that require a render (contrast ratios computed from live backgrounds, overflow, layout at viewport widths) as if they were verified. Needs verification section should be substantial. Should offer the one thing that unlocks the rest: obscura on PATH, with the one-line install. Must NOT suggest Playwright, Puppeteer, chrome-headless-shell, chrome-devtools-mcp or browser-use — those are removed and recommending one is wrong advice.
assertions: States explicitly that rendered verification did not happen
Reports no finding that requires a render (measured overflow, live-background contrast, per-viewport layout) as verified
Needs verification section lists the checks that the missing browser blocked
Offers a concrete way to unlock the rendered checks — installing obscura, with the command or release name, not merely a statement that a browser is needed
Does NOT suggest installing or using Playwright, Puppeteer, chrome-headless-shell, chrome-devtools-mcp, Playwright MCP, browser-use or claude-in-chrome
Does not silently pass on categories it could not test

evals.name: clean-surface-restraint
evals.prompt: Review this component for design issues: skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/clean-card.html
evals.expected_output: The fixture is deliberately well-built — tokens, states, focus-visible, correct contrast, tracked caps, tabular numerals. A good review returns a clean verdict and a short report, does not invent findings to fill sections, and still produces a non-empty Needs verification. Padding this report with Low-severity nits is the failure mode being tested. It must also prove it looked: 'clean' and 'not reviewed' produce nearly the same report, so the review has to name what it verified.
assertions: Returns a clean verdict with zero Blocker and zero High findings
Does not report a contrast failure (the fixture passes at 15.3:1 and 6.29:1)
Does not report a focus failure (the fixture uses :focus-visible with a 2px ring)
Does not report a target-size failure (targets are 44px min-height)
Does not report a spacing-scale failure (4px half-step on an 8px base is on-scale)

Names at least three specific things it checked and found correct, with values — the tokens, the :focus-visible ring, the tracked caps at 0.96px, the tabular numerals, or measured ratios. Without this the eval cannot tell 'reviewed and found nothing' from 'did not review', and a reply of 'looks fine to me' would pass
Quotes contrast as a numerator over a denominator, so a clean result carries the population it was clean across
Total finding count is 5 or fewer
Needs verification section is present and non-empty
Any observation offered is framed as a judgment call or open question, not as a defect

evals.name: scoped-diff-review
evals.prompt: I just changed the pricing page hero and the plan cards. Give it a design pass before I show my team — don't review the whole site, just what I touched.
evals.expected_output: Should hold scope to the named surfaces, propose the recent-changes diff rather than sweeping the codebase, and say in one line if it notices something adjacent rather than expanding the review. Tests the scope discipline in stage 0.
assertions: Holds scope to the pricing hero and plan cards
Proposes reading the recent diff rather than sweeping the whole codebase
Mentions any adjacent issue in one line without expanding the review into it
Does not produce findings about unrelated pages or components

evals.name: imitation-material-rules-fire
evals.prompt: Run the source scanner over skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/imitation-material.css and tell me what it found.
evals.expected_output: stacked-inset-bevel fires twice (.spec-plate, .key-cap) and letterpress-text-shadow fires three times (.engraved-title, .debossed-label, .stamped-mark), both as Tier 2. Neither fires on the silent half: layered elevation, glass with one inset highlight, an inset focus ring, an inset hairline, and blurred legibility text-shadows. This is the artifact that proves the two rules can fail; a run reporting 0 hits means a regex regressed, not that the file is clean.
assertions: Reports stacked-inset-bevel with 2 hits
Reports letterpress-text-shadow with 3 hits
Both are reported at Tier 2, not as blocking gates
Does not report either rule against the layered .card shadow or the .glass inset highlight
Does not report letterpress-text-shadow against the blurred .hero-caption or .overlay-text shadows

evals.name: coverage-contract-multi-surface
evals.prompt: Review the design and UX of our admin app before we hand it to a human. It's 11 screens; the dev server is on localhost:3000 and the routes are in src/router.tsx.
evals.expected_output: Should enumerate all 11 surfaces at stage 0 from the router and write a worklist ledger before capturing anything, rather than discovering screens as it goes. The pipeline runs per surface, so finishing stages 2-8 on screen 1 is one row, not the review. If it stops short it must say so in the shape the skill requires ('4 of 11 surfaces reviewed, resuming at 5'), carry the fraction in the verdict line, and leave the ledger on disk — never compress 11 screens of scope into a 4-screen report that reads as finished. Tests the coverage contract, which exists because reviews have shipped covering 3 of 14 screens and reviews have written the report after only the gate and render stages.
assertions: Enumerates every surface in scope before capturing, deriving the list from the router rather than discovering screens incrementally
Writes a worklist/ledger to the workdir and updates it as stages complete
Treats stages 2-8 as running per surface rather than once for the whole app
The verdict line carries the surface fraction, including when coverage is complete
Any stop short of the full worklist is declared with a resume point, not absorbed silently
If it samples deliberately, states which surfaces, the basis, and what the sample cannot speak for

evals.name: worklist-gate-blocks-partial-report
evals.prompt: Review our admin app — 6 screens, dev server on localhost:3000. I only have time for the first couple of screens today.
evals.expected_output: Should still enumerate all 6 surfaces with worklist.py init at stage 0, because the denominator is fixed by scope not by available time. Should run worklist.py check before writing anything, get a non-zero exit, and respond by declaring the stop with a resume point ('2 of 6 surfaces reviewed, resuming at 3') in the reply, the verdict line and the Coverage block — not by writing a full-shaped report over open cells, and not by silently redefining scope to 2 surfaces. The ledger stays on disk so a later session continues. Alternatively it may propose a declared sample with a stated basis, which is a finished review of the sample.
assertions: Runs worklist.py init with all 6 surfaces even though only 2 will be reviewed
Runs worklist.py check before writing the report and treats the non-zero exit as blocking
Declares the stop with a resume point rather than absorbing the reduced scope
Verdict line carries the surface fraction
Does not redefine the worklist down to the surfaces it managed to reach
Leaves the ledger on disk and says where it is

evals.name: band-voids-and-unread-tokens
evals.prompt: Review skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/band-voids.html. Its control is band-voids-clean.html — the same five bands with every defect removed. Tell me what is wrong with the first one and prove your probes did not just fire on both.
evals.expected_output: Three Tier 1 findings plus the denominator discipline. (1) The page has no <title> — WCAG 2.4.2 Page Titled, Level A. (2) Three bands are voids: #dead paints no ink inside 220px of shell, #thin holds one line inside 400px, #foot fills roughly 11% of its box. The band-seam table should be quoted, showing ink-to-ink gaps in the hundreds of pixels against the control's flat 84px. (3) --accent-on-dark is declared on :root and referenced by no rule, so nothing on the page is painted with it. The report must quote contrast as failures OVER examined, not failures alone, and must state that the control returned zero voids and zero unconsumed tokens — otherwise 'the probes fired' and 'the probes are miscalibrated' are the same output.
assertions: Flags the missing <title> as a WCAG 2.4.2 Level A failure
Reports the #dead band as rendering no ink while occupying its own margins
Reports #thin as near-empty and #foot as low-fill, or equivalent, with measured ink and box heights
Reports --accent-on-dark as declared and consumed by no rule, and does NOT report --canvas (which is consumed via a shorthand and is a known false-positive shape)
Quotes contrast as a numerator over a denominator (failures over examined), never as a bare failure count
States that the clean control returned zero voids and zero unconsumed tokens, as evidence the probes discriminate
Does not report the two healthy bands (#hero, #close) as voids

evals.name: implicit-grid-tracks
evals.prompt: Review skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/implicit-tracks.html. Its control is implicit-tracks-clean.html — the same index rows with both defects removed. Tell me what is wrong with the first one and prove your probes did not just fire on both.
evals.expected_output: Two layout-integrity findings plus the discrimination evidence. (1) .idx__a declares four columns and renders five children, so grid-auto-flow puts the trailing arrow on an implicit second row: computed grid-template-rows reads two tracks where one was intended, on all four rows (repeatedInstances: 4), and removing the orphan track takes each row from 81px to 57px. (2) Every row's date cell is an empty measuring 0x0 — an element emitted for a field the record does not carry, with the .idx--undated variant that would drop the column present in the stylesheet and applied by nothing. The report must state that the control returned zero spilledRows and zero emptyCells, and must NOT report the four-card / three-column .cards grid on either page: equal columns mean wrapping is intended and a ragged last row is a layout decision.
assertions: Reports the implicit second grid row on .idx__a, quoting the computed grid-template-rows and the four-columns-versus-five-children count
Names the repetition (every row of the group), not a single instance
Reports the zero-sized .idx__m date cell and identifies the empty datetime attribute
Notes that the .idx--undated variant exists in the stylesheet and is selected by nothing
States that the clean control returned zero spilled rows and zero empty cells, as evidence the probes discriminate
Does not report the healthy .cards grid, whose ragged last row is intentional wrapping

evals.name: divider-gutter-and-clipping
evals.prompt: Review skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/divider-gutter.html. Its control is divider-gutter-clean.html — the same layout with the gutters corrected. divider-clipped.html is a third case. Tell me what is wrong with the first one and prove your probes did not just fire on all three.
evals.expected_output: The divider-proximity findings, plus the discrimination evidence, plus one honest limit. probeDividerProximity measures ink-to-rule gaps against a 16px floor and a 24px target, and the defective fixture sets text hard against a vertical rule. The clean control must return zero violations below the floor. divider-clipped.html carries a documented Obscura under-report, so the review must say the clipped count is a floor rather than a census rather than quoting it as complete. This eval exists because these three fixtures were the only orphans in the set — the newest layout probe was the one with no eval, and its output was summed by no consumer, so a surface whose only defect was a divider gutter printed layoutFindingCount: 0 on the first line a reviewer reads.
assertions: Reports at least one divider-proximity violation on divider-gutter.html with a measured ink-to-rule gap in px and the floor it breached
States that the clean control returned zero violations below the floor, as evidence the probe discriminates
The run summary's layout finding count is non-zero for the defective fixture — a divider-only defect must not print as 0 layout findings
Distinguishes the 16px floor from the 24px target, rather than treating anything under 24px as a failure
On divider-clipped.html, states that clipped-text detection under-reports on this engine, so the count is a floor and not a census
Reports the repetition as a count where the defect repeats, rather than one row per instance

evals.name: claims-must-trace-to-the-run
evals.prompt: I've got a review workdir at review-work/ from an earlier run, and a draft report at review-work/report.md. Before I send it, check the report's numbers are actually supported by the run.
evals.expected_output: Should run `python scripts/audit_run.py claims review-work/ --report review-work/report.md`, treat a non-zero exit as blocking, and report which specific claims the run does not support — with the manifest's own figure beside each. Must not soften the wording of an unsupported claim to get past the gate; the fix is to correct the number or take the measurement. Also should run `audit_run.py capability` and report which metrics are unmeasurable on this engine rather than quoting them as counts. This is the anti-fabrication gate: a model completing the shape of a review will supply a plausible count, and the point of the gate is that the count now costs something. The canonical case is a report claiming it audited 47 buttons when the component inventory counted 9.
assertions: Runs audit_run.py claims against the report and the workdir, not a manual read of the numbers
Treats a non-zero exit as blocking rather than advisory
Names each unsupported claim with both the claimed figure and the figure the run recorded
Does not resolve an unsupported claim by rewording it more vaguely — the fix is the number or the measurement
Also runs the capability audit and reports which metrics are unmeasurable rather than printing them as zeros
Does not invent a passing result for a workdir or report that does not exist — says so instead

evals.name: runner-completes-and-marks-the-ledger
evals.prompt: Review the design of skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/landing.html across the full viewport matrix, and keep the coverage ledger current as you go rather than filling it in at the end.
evals.expected_output: The capture sweep must complete every viewport and mark the ledger's gates and render cells automatically. Measured on the previous build 18 Aug 2026: run_review.py died with `KeyError: 'exceedsThreshold'` at line 725 on the FIRST viewport of every run, because `_layout_finding_count` indexed `L["rails"]["exceedsThreshold"]` while `probeSharedRails()` had an early return emitting only `{clusters, disagreementPx}`. SKILL.md's stage 2 warns against exactly that two sections above the script committing it — 'assert against the probe's actual return shape' — and the crash left a workdir that looked like a partial capture rather than a failure. There was also no working path to automatic ledger marking at all: SKILL.md documented `run_review.py --worklist --surface`, the Python runner crashed before reaching it, and the Node runner had no such flag, so all eight cells had to be set by hand. This eval is the regression guard for both.
assertions: The capture sweep completes every viewport in the matrix without a traceback, and the workdir holds one probe JSON per viewport
No probe's early-return shape causes a consumer to raise — a missing key contributes nothing rather than killing the run
The ledger's gates and render cells for this surface are marked by the runner via --worklist, not by hand
Cells the capture does not prove — states, inventory, craft, flow, system, intent — remain open after the sweep
If any probe did not run, the summary names it and the manifest records null rather than zero

evals.name: a-blind-sub-check-must-not-read-as-clean
evals.prompt: Review skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/landing.html. For the layout-integrity pass specifically, tell me for each sub-check whether it found nothing or could not see anything, and how you know the difference.
evals.expected_output: The point of this eval is the distinction, not the findings. Measured on the previous build 18 Aug 2026: 12 of 13 layout-integrity sub-checks returned 0 at all seven viewports, and two of those zeros sat over real computable defects — a five-way left-rail disagreement measured at 15/43/32/32/0/24px, and a hero at 30% fill with a 747px void. Both were working exactly as documented and blind to the defect anyway: `rails` clusters only h1-h3 and excludes card interiors, and `deadSpace` needs a row while the hero is a column. Nothing in the output let a reader tell a scope-limited zero from a clean surface. A good answer states each sub-check's scope beside its zero, names the two that are structurally blind on this surface, and does not present the aggregate layout count as evidence the layout is sound. The `dividerProximity` sub-check is the other half: on the previous build it returned 15 violations at >=1024 of which zero were real, each naming a hero button's own 1px border as the divider and its own label as the encroaching ink, including a geometrically impossible gapPx of -139.5. It must now report zero violations on this fixture and say how many side borders it excluded as box outlines.
assertions: Reports the layout sub-checks individually rather than as a single aggregate count
For each sub-check returning zero, states what population it examined, so a scope-limited zero is distinguishable from a clean surface
Names at least one sub-check that is structurally blind on this surface and says why — rails clustering only h1-h3, or deadSpace requiring a row where the hero is a column
Does not offer the layout finding count as evidence that the layout is sound
Reports zero divider-proximity violations on this fixture, and names the count of side borders excluded as box outlines rather than dividers
Reports no negative gap measurement — a negative distance is recorded as a crossing, not as the worst violation on the page
Where a sub-check's scope means a real defect would be missed, that limit appears in Needs verification rather than only in the reviewer's reasoning
